To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the industry's financial support of medical education has grown substantially in the past decade; (ii) the industry's support is concentrated in a few areas; (iii) there are no clear patterns in the distribution of support by academic medical centers; and (iv) the industry's funding of continuing medical education (CME) is more than double the amount of its funding of other types of educational activities.

(a) industry support for CME is substantial, with the largest portion of funding provided by the pharmaceutical industry and the largest portion of the industry's support directed to the support of physicians' education, and (b) industry support for physicians' education is increasing at a faster pace than industry support for other educational programs and activities, such as the education of students and residents, as well as for research.
